recent_posts.title: Everything we announced at Sessions 2026
recent_posts.summary: Stripe announced 288 new products and features at its annual Sessions 2026 conference. Key highlights include an expanded Agentic Commerce Suite with Meta and Google partnerships enabling AI agent-driven purchases, a new Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) for agent microtransactions, Checkout Studio with AI-assisted optimization and A/B testing, major Radar fraud detection upgrades including bot abuse prevention and custom fraud models, usage-based billing enhancements via Metronome, a Stripe Database offering real-time Postgres access, Treasury expansion to Australia and Canada with stablecoin support, a Stripe card with 2% cashback, Global Payouts to 100+ countries, Issuing for AI agents, and a public product roadmap through Q1 2027. The announcements span payments, revenue management, money management, embedded finance, and crypto/stablecoin infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: Giving agents the ability to pay
recent_posts.summary: Stripe is launching Link's wallet for agents, a new product that gives AI agents programmatic access to payment credentials without exposing raw card data. Built on Stripe's new Issuing for agents, it allows agents to request one-time-use virtual cards or Shared Payment Tokens (SPTs) backed by a user's existing Link wallet. Consumers approve each spend request via web or mobile app. For developers building consumer-facing agents, it removes the need to build wallet infrastructure from scratch. Businesses can also use Stripe Issuing for agents directly to build custom agentic wallets, set spending controls, automate business spend, and manage fund flows for use cases like fintech, vertical SaaS, and marketplaces.

recent_posts.title: How agents, digital wallets, and trust are rewriting checkout
recent_posts.summary: Analysis of checkout trends across nearly 20,000 B2C businesses on Stripe's network reveals several key shifts: mobile now dominates even high-value purchases; digital wallets cut mobile checkout time in half but preferred wallets vary by region and generation; localization is critical as irrelevant payment methods can reduce conversion by up to 15% while offering the right local method (e.g., BLIK in Poland) can boost it by 46%; and AI agents are beginning to reshape the purchase path, requiring checkout to handle identity verification and agent-authorized transactions. Stripe's AI-driven fraud tools can reduce fraud by 30% without hurting conversion.

recent_posts.title: Insights from Shoptalk 2026: How agents are changing retail
recent_posts.summary: Shoptalk 2026 surfaced three key themes around agentic commerce in retail: the need for a standard framework as brands experiment with AI-driven discovery, the expansion of agentic experiences beyond chat into native checkout and third-party surfaces, and the growing importance of brand trust as AI commoditizes product comparison. Retailers like Sephora, New Balance, and Tapestry shared live examples of loyalty data personalization, direct product feeds for AI discoverability, and brand investment strategies. Stripe promoted its Agentic Commerce Suite as infrastructure for syndicating product catalogs across AI surfaces and optimizing checkout conversion in agent-driven journeys.

recent_posts.title: How Stripe Radar helps prevent free trial abuse
recent_posts.summary: Stripe Radar now includes a one-click free trial abuse prevention feature powered by an AI model trained on payment instrument, device, and payment history data across Stripe's network. The tool detects abusive behaviors like repeated trial signups and invalid payment methods with 90% accuracy. Free trial abuse has grown 6.2x from November 2025 to February 2026, with AI companies being disproportionately targeted due to expensive compute costs. In its first two months, the feature blocked over 550,000 high-risk trials across four AI businesses, preventing an estimated $4.4 million in losses. The solution is available to all businesses, not just AI companies.

recent_posts.title: Three of the biggest fraud trends from MRC Vegas 2026
recent_posts.summary: At MRC Vegas 2026, fraud leaders highlighted three major trends reshaping fraud prevention. First, top teams are moving away from universal authentication toward dynamic, intent-based friction—only challenging the riskiest 1% of users rather than all customers. Second, agentic commerce is breaking rules-based fraud detection, requiring fraud logic to be embedded directly in payment infrastructure to handle real-time AI-driven transactions. Third, generative AI has made deepfakes and synthetic identities trivially easy to produce, forcing identity verification to rely on multilayered checks and anomaly detection rather than any single signal. Stripe's Radar adaptive 3DS, Shared Payment Tokens, and Stripe Identity are cited as tools addressing each of these challenges.

recent_posts.title: Testing the impact of Adaptive Pricing across 1.5M subscription checkout sessions
recent_posts.summary: Stripe's Adaptive Pricing for subscriptions is now generally available, automatically presenting prices in customers' local currencies across 150+ countries while Stripe handles FX conversion and renewal consistency. An A/B test across 1.5 million subscription checkout sessions showed a 4.7% increase in conversion rate, 1.9% improvement in authorization rate, and 5.4% higher lifetime value per session on average. A stability buffer keeps renewal amounts consistent despite exchange rate fluctuations. Over 500,000 businesses including Cursor, Perplexity, and Runway already use the feature.

recent_posts.title: Introducing the Machine Payments Protocol
recent_posts.summary: Stripe and Tempo have co-launched the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), an open standard enabling AI agents to make payments programmatically without human intervention. MPP supports microtransactions, recurring payments, stablecoins, fiat via cards, and buy now pay later methods through Shared Payment Tokens. Stripe merchants can accept agent payments using the existing PaymentIntents API in a few lines of code, with full support for tax, fraud protection, and reporting. Early adopters include Browserbase (pay-per-session browser infrastructure), PostalForm (physical mail), and Prospect Butcher Co. (food delivery). MPP is part of Stripe's broader Agentic Commerce Suite alongside ACP and MCP integrations.

recent_posts.title: 10 lessons from building agentic commerce infrastructure at Stripe
recent_posts.summary: Stripe shares 10 lessons from building the first generation of agentic commerce infrastructure, covering the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) and Agentic Commerce Suite. Key insights include: product catalog fragmentation across AI agents, the need for real-time inventory verification, protocol volatility and zombie integrations, Shared Payment Tokens (SPTs) as a secure payment primitive, near-zero fraud rates leveraging the Stripe network, starting with a focused SKU set, brand control challenges on third-party AI surfaces, identity and loyalty gaps in guest-checkout-like agentic flows, the first-party vs. third-party agent strategy, and emerging machine-to-machine payments using stablecoins for pay-per-call models.

recent_posts.title: Analyzing first-party fraud trends: Account, free trial, and refund abuse
recent_posts.summary: Stripe analyzed hundreds of millions of transactions to identify three fast-growing types of first-party fraud: account/multiaccount abuse, free trial abuse, and refund fraud. Key findings include 7.4% of AI company sign-ups implicated in multiaccount abuse, a 6.2x increase in abusive free trials from November 2025 to February 2026, and an estimated $100 billion in annual global losses from refund abuse. AI companies are disproportionately affected due to compute costs tied to usage and reliance on free trials for customer acquisition. Traditional prevention methods like blocking virtual cards no longer work effectively. Stripe is rolling out new Radar features to address each fraud type, including a 90%-accurate free trial abuse predictor and early-access programs for account abuse and refund abuse detection.
